current_evidence: Not verified. The shared WebFetch budget ran out (proxy HTTP 403) before the council's 'Make a planning application' page or the PDF could be fetched. A web search turned up only the August 2023 v2 checklist and this February 2024 BNG-addendum version (plus the April 2023 draft consultation), so nothing newer was found, but the page that links it could not be checked.

issues.detail: Gloucestershire CC is a county planning authority: it handles minerals and waste county matters and its own Regulation 3 development. Grokbot reads the general checklist as a district-style list and puts about 25 requirements under 'Full planning' with 'INFERRED' notes. It shows '(none)' for 'County own devt (Reg 3)', even though it read Appendix 3 'Checklist for the submission of applications for Regulation (Reg 3) development'. It also fills 'Minerals & waste (county)' only from Appendix 2 (waste). The Appendix 1 minerals checklist it read is not reflected separately.
issues.evidence: docs_read includes appendix-3-checklist-for-the-submission-of-applications-for-regulation-reg-3-development.docx and appendix-1-checklist-for-the-submission-of-applications-for-minerals-development.docx; app_type_rows 'County own devt (Reg 3)': '(none)'

issues.detail: Householder, Listed building consent, Advertisement consent, Lawful development cert, Works to trees, Permission in principle and similar rows say 'national requirements only'. A county planning authority does not determine these application types, so these rows should be marked not applicable rather than implying there are no local requirements.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows Householder: 'No specific local requirements identified for this application type ... national requirements only (check source)'

issues.detail: Many requirement labels carry trigger text from a different checklist entry or from 'further guidance' reference lists. 'Archaeological Assessment' quotes drainage guidance (Approved Document Part H, BS6297). 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' actually quotes the Hydrological or Hydrogeological Assessment trigger. 'Design and Access Statement' quotes a waste-minimisation fragment ('temporary buildings is proposed and will be transported off site'). 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' quotes the Tree Survey trigger. 'Transport Assessment' and 'Travel Plan' both quote the Construction Management Plan trigger. 'Ventilation / Extraction (odour)' quotes the Statement of Pre-application Engagement trigger. 'Coal Mining' quotes only reference titles. 'Block plan / Site plan' quotes 'England's website Planning for Sport for advice.' 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' (not a county requirement) quotes ALC references plus the Land Contamination trigger.
issues.evidence: Transport Assessment row: '...Active Travel England guidance 12 Document When is it required? Construction Management Plan Any development unless the Highways Authority has indicated that one would not be required.'

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut-off fragments that do not say when the item is required. BNG: 'least 10% BNG.' Ecological Survey: 'location of protected species is given.' EIA: 'that no EIA is required.' Daylight/Sunlight: 'no undue overshadowing to the waterway.' Open space: 'open space/playing fields, common land or village greens.' Contaminated land: '...why a Phase 1 Contamination Risk Assessment is not required...'. Site levels: 'Any development which involves any change in ground levels or where topography or Redacted versions for publicity may be required...' (two entries merged). Pre-application advice: 'Plan (CEMP) Pre-application advice may be sought from the Highways Authority'.

Requirements named in Grokbot's own extracted text have no row of their own. From the general checklist: Hydrological or Hydrogeological Assessment (any development involving materials or processes that could pollute the water environment), Statement of Pre-application Engagement or Consultation (e.g. where a boundary is shared with a sensitive receptor), Dust Management Plan, and Waste Minimisation Statement (Waste Core Strategy WCS2 / Waste Minimisation SPD). From the waste checklist: Green Belt Assessment, Ancient Woodland Assessment, Assessment of impact on railway level crossings, Delivery and Servicing Management Plan, Road Safety Audit Stage 1 and Designer's Response, Utilities Assessment, Water Framework Directive compliance assessment, Inshore and Offshore Marine Plan compliance assessment, Soil Resources Assessment, Unstable Land Assessment, Geodiversity Assessment, Waste Needs Assessment and Restoration Scheme. The reference row claims 82 requirement items, but only about 25 distinct requirements appear.
issues.evidence: Waste appendix excerpts: 'Geological, land and soils assessment Coal Mining Risk Assessment Soil Resources Assessment Land Contamination Assessment Unstable Land Assessment Geodiversity Assessment'; 'Design And Access Statement Waste Minimisation Statement Waste Needs Assessment'

issues.detail: Identical trigger text is reused under different requirement names. 'Agricultural / rural workers' dwelling appraisal' and 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' are word-for-word identical. 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan', 'Transport Assessment' and 'Travel Plan' all carry the CMP trigger. 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment' and 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' both carry the Tree Survey trigger.
issues.evidence: Both agricultural rows: 'agricultural land Agricultural Land Classification: protecting the best and most versatile agricultural land (NE, 2009) ...'

issues.detail: The tab_items are mostly process or boilerplate text, not local requirements: two GDPR/personal-data publication notices, a 'Further information and guidance Planning Practice Guidance (PPG) Making an application...' header run-on, and a garbled merge of the site-levels trigger with a protected-species redaction note.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'Personal data and planning applications Please note that with the exception of the applicant's contact details ... may be published on the Council's website.'

issues.detail: The sources are mixed. tab_items cite the August 2023 v2 checklist (updated-revised-gcc-local-validation-checklist-v2-final-version-rd-check-aug-2023.pdf), while the reference row and app_type_rows cite the February 2024 BNG-addendum version. The list date 2024-02-01 is taken from the URL ('feb-2024'), not from the document text, and could not be confirmed.

summary: Neither the current-version status nor the contents could be verified live because the shared WebFetch budget ran out. A search found nothing newer than this February 2024 BNG-addendum checklist. Grokbot's own excerpts show it treated a county minerals/waste/Reg 3 list like a district list. It ignored the Reg 3 and minerals appendices, attached many triggers to the wrong requirement or cut them to fragments, and dropped several named requirements (e.g. Waste Minimisation Statement, Hydrogeological Assessment, Geodiversity, Green Belt).
